A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CB-LLMs study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A and B are readable and support direct comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification and generation experiments, MTurk evaluations, and concept-unlearning and toxicity-reduction results in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark scores, human evaluations, and intervention case studies in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The classification pipeline and generation architecture, objectives, and adversarial training procedure are retained. Equation (7) completes the expression for the already specified negative-entropy objective; it does not establish a changed training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use SST2, Yelp Polarity, AGnews, and DBpedia for classification and generation, plus ToxicDPOqa and toxic-chat for the chatbot case study. Task and scenario coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same TBM&C3M implementation, fine-tuned black-box models, and method variants. Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2, 5–7, and 12.

E3.justification: Reported backbones, sample restrictions, metrics, intervention settings, and human-evaluation procedures are unchanged. This includes the generation setup in Section 4.2 and the survey design in Appendix A.7.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the ACC, sparse-final-layer, and adversarial-training ablations, concept-unlearning and toxicity case studies, and appendix neuron and explanation analyses. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three different workers evaluating each survey question. Neither introduces additional run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results match throughout Tables 2–8 and 12, including the human-study and generation scores. The qualitative examples, intervention outcomes, and appendix explanation tables also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (7) replaces the unreduced p log p expression with an explicit sum over p_k log p_k and defines p_k as a probability-vector entry. This corrects the missing class reduction in the formal scalar-loss definition. Other mathematical content is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable intrinsic interpretability, competitive performance, steerability, concept unlearning, and toxicity reduction.

C2.justification: Interpretations of ACC, adversarial disentanglement, generation quality, and concept interventions are unchanged. The discussions of concept coverage and potential overreliance on unsupervised neurons also remain the same.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters, runtime information, prompt templates, survey details, and the code-access link are retained. The added acknowledgment credits funding and computing support without supplying new implementation specifications or reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2's research positioning and all 22 cited works are retained. References 17–19 move from page 11 to page 12 because of the acknowledgment insertion.

P1.justification: v4 adds an acknowledgment before the references, explains the probability entry in Equation (7), and changes Appendix A.8's reference from '11' to 'Table 11'. The narrative and section organization otherwise remain stable.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment changes the reference-page layout, and Equation (7) has a revised display. Figures 1–16 and Tables 1–12 retain their content, structure, and placement, with only small typesetting differences.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves mathematical precision by making Equation (7)'s class reduction explicit and improves navigation by correcting the Table 11 reference. The empirical evidence and substantive scientific conclusions remain unchanged, so the overall benefit is limited.
